project.title: BUS311 Individual Company Capstone
project.subtitle: One company. One financial decision.
project.companyEligibility: Choose one U.S.-listed public company with usable public financial statements.
project.audience: The selected company's CFO and Board
project.decision: Recommend one growth/efficiency investment or working-capital improvement, compared with the status quo.

finalSubmission.deadlineLabel: Monday, Nov. 30, 2026 at 12:30 p.m. ET, when class begins

hub.purpose: Use company evidence and an Excel model to recommend one financial decision.
hub.centralQuestion: Should this company make the proposed change, and under what conditions?

stages.label: Stage 1
stages.title: Choose a company and decision
stages.work: Complete Start: company, ticker, a short company snapshot, one FactSet learning and feature used, and one tentative decision.
stages.submit: Upload the continuing workbook with Start complete.
stages.grade: Company and snapshot 2; specific FactSet learning 1; a plausible tentative decision 2.

stages.label: Stage 2
stages.title: Explain sales and the decision
stages.work: Complete Revenue and Sources: three comparable years of sales, two drivers, one peer comparison, two risks, and one forecast claim.
stages.submit: Upload the same workbook with Revenue and Sources updated.
stages.grade: Revenue history 2; two drivers 2; peer and risks 2; forecast claim and sources 2.
stages.hours: About 3–4 focused hours, including class work.

stages.label: Stage 3
stages.title: Model, challenge, and revise
stages.work: Complete Model, Sources, and Revision. Compare base, upside, and downside NPV; vary one important assumption; check one meaningful challenge and record your judgment.
stages.submit: Upload the same workbook. The challenge record is inside it; there is no separate revision assignment.
stages.grade: Cash-flow model and assumptions 4; scenarios and sensitivity 4; verified challenge and judgment 4.
stages.hours: About 4–6 focused hours, including the worked example and class support.

stages.label: Stage 4
stages.title: Recommend and present
stages.dateLabel: PowerPoint: November 30 at 12:30 p.m. ET; presentations: November 30–December 9
stages.work: Use six core slides to explain your decision, evidence, numbers, risks, and next step. Put supporting calculations and sources in an optional appendix.
stages.submit: Upload one editable PowerPoint, then present that file live. Up to 7 minutes presenting and 3 minutes answering questions.
stages.hours: About 3–4 focused hours to prepare and rehearse.

decisionPaths.title: Growth or efficiency investment
decisionPaths.question: Should the company fund a specific capacity, technology, or process improvement?
decisionPaths.method: Incremental after-tax cash flow and NPV versus doing nothing.
decisionPaths.inputs: Initial equipment and setup cash cost; annual additional sales or cost savings; operating costs; tax; additional working capital; end-of-project recovery. Use a bounded five-year project. Explain any estimated project cost using a public benchmark.
decisionPaths.boundary: Choose a project with a defensible public cost benchmark. A whole-company acquisition, buyback, debt restructuring, or full enterprise valuation is outside this project.

decisionPaths.title: Working-capital improvement
decisionPaths.question: Should the company reduce cash tied up in inventory or receivables without damaging service or sales?
decisionPaths.method: Incremental cash released, implementation and operating costs, and NPV versus current practice.
decisionPaths.inputs: For receivables, annual sales / 365 × days reduced; for inventory, annual cost of goods sold / 365 × days reduced. Use one lever. Count the release once, explain the duration, and include restoration if the improvement ends.
decisionPaths.boundary: Use one cash-conversion lever, with two service or revenue risks. Do not count the same cash release again as operating revenue or recurring savings.

feedback.revision: Revise the existing Stage 3 Canvas submission within seven calendar days of written feedback. The higher score replaces the original. If feedback arrives November 11, the revision window ends November 18. No separate revision file or assignment is required.
feedback.support: Before the November 4 model deadline, use the Example tab and the short model instructions. The template calculates discounting and NPV; explain those calculations in your own words. Plan a model workshop before submission.
feedback.finalModel: If feedback changes your numbers, replace the workbook in the original Stage 3 assignment and use that version in the slides. Identify the workbook version and model cell below each financial result.

policies.individualWork: Research, assumptions, formulas, writing, and presentation are individual work. You must explain the submitted analysis yourself.
policies.stageOne: Stage 1 is exploration. Use web research and/or AI plus FactSet. Name one FactSet learning and the feature used. Formal citations and proof are not required until Stage 2. The decision may change as the evidence develops.
policies.sources: From Stage 2, use one Sources tab. Record a source ID, exact SEC filing/table or FactSet report/metric, link or report locator, date and period, units, and the fact or assumption used. Put that ID beside the input or claim. Explain changed definitions or missing evidence where they matter.
policies.factSetPermission: Students and the instructor may use FactSet evidence in BUS311 course deliverables. Raw exports and screenshots remain in approved course-restricted systems and are not committed publicly or uploaded to public AI tools.
policies.challenge: Complete one challenge before the Stage 3 submission. Use AI, a peer, or the provided self-review questions. Record the strongest challenge, what you checked, and what you changed or why you kept the original conclusion. AI output is not financial evidence.
policies.aiPrivacy: Give public AI tools only a short summary you wrote from public information. Do not upload workbooks, raw FactSet exports or screenshots, personal information, private teaching material, or nonpublic information. If AI is used, name the tool and purpose in Revision and disclose it briefly in the presentation appendix or source notes.
policies.missingEvidence: Use the required minimum where evidence supports it. If no defensible peer or comparable historical figure exists, state why and discuss an appropriate limitation or proxy with the instructor. Never invent company facts. Label estimated project inputs as assumptions and explain their basis.
policies.lateWork: Milestones remain eligible under the BUS311 syllabus late-work policy. A late milestone delays feedback and can make dependent project work harder; complete missing milestone work before relying on it in a later stage. Documented exceptions follow the applicable college and course process.
policies.revision: Stages 1–3 may each be revised once within seven calendar days of written feedback. Replace the workbook in the original assignment; the higher score replaces the original. Summarize the change in Revision.
policies.finalFileLock: The PowerPoint company-analysis project file is due Monday, Nov. 30, 2026 at 12:30 p.m. ET, when class begins. The submitted .pptx locks at that time for every student regardless of Oral Presentation date. Only instructor-authorized accessibility or file-repair corrections that do not alter the analysis or recommendation are permitted afterward.
policies.absence: Approved documented absences use the next protected slot or instructor-scheduled make-up. The live Oral Presentation, including responses to questions, remains required. Unexcused absences follow the BUS311 late-work policy and still require a make-up Oral Presentation.
policies.submission: Submit the continuing workbook at Stages 1, 2, and 3. Submit one editable .pptx at Stage 4. The Oral Presentation uses that same deck; no second final file is required. Canvas supplies the live upload links and presentation order.

challengePrompts: What assumption could most easily make this decision unattractive?
What independent evidence or calculation would test that concern?
After checking, what will you change, or why will you keep your original conclusion?

slideOutline.title: What should the company do?
slideOutline.prompt: State the company, your name, the proposed action, and one clear recommendation.
slideOutline.evidence: One sentence naming the decision and its scope.
slideOutline.notes: About 45 seconds. Lead with your recommendation; identify the status quo.

slideOutline.title: Why this decision?
slideOutline.prompt: Explain the business need and how the company makes money.
slideOutline.evidence: A simple three-year sales chart and two drivers.
slideOutline.notes: About 60 seconds. Connect sales or cash conversion to the proposed action.

slideOutline.title: What evidence supports it?
slideOutline.prompt: Show the decisive evidence and the assumption it supports.
slideOutline.evidence: One peer comparison, one forecast claim, and source IDs.
slideOutline.notes: About 60 seconds. Separate reported facts from your estimate.

slideOutline.title: What do the numbers show?
slideOutline.prompt: Compare doing nothing with the change in base, upside, and downside cases.
slideOutline.evidence: Three scenario NPVs, one sensitivity, and the model version/cells.
slideOutline.notes: About 90 seconds. Explain initial cash flow, annual cash flow, and discounting. The status quo has zero incremental NPV.

slideOutline.title: What could go wrong?
slideOutline.prompt: Explain two risks, the strongest challenge, and what you changed.
slideOutline.evidence: One observable condition that would change your recommendation.
slideOutline.notes: About 60 seconds. Acknowledge uncertainty without hiding the decision.

slideOutline.title: What happens next?
slideOutline.prompt: Name the first action, responsible role, timing, and one measure to monitor.
slideOutline.evidence: A practical next step and a stop, review, or expand trigger.
slideOutline.notes: About 45 seconds. Restate the requested decision. Leave time for transitions.

example.decision: Install order-handling equipment for a five-year project.
drivers: More customer orders support higher sales.
Faster order handling may reduce labor cost per order.
example.peer: Fictional Dockside Supply sales grew 8% in 2025; Harbor grew 10%. Both use calendar years and the same currency.
example.claim: If the new equipment reduces handling time without raising errors, Harbor can save $3 million annually for five years. Reject this assumption if the pilot savings fall below the break-even level.
example.challenge: The vendor saving estimate may overstate achievable labor savings.
example.verification: Recalculate NPV using $2.2 million annual savings, then compare the required saving with a pilot measurement.
example.judgment: Recommend a pilot before full commitment. Base NPV is positive but the downside is negative; expand only if observed annualized savings exceed the break-even amount.
example.source: All company names, historical figures, and assumptions in this example are fictional teaching data. They are not a student company solution.
annotations: Three years and two drivers establish enough context to explain the decision.
The $8 million cost and annual savings are labeled assumptions, not reported company facts.
Annual depreciation is $8 million / 5 years; taxable operating savings are reduced by depreciation.
The model compares incremental cash flow with doing nothing. It discounts cash received later.
The downside and break-even test reveal what evidence would change the recommendation.
